lens: Radix Themes: elegant defaults, accessible, low design debt
name: Radix Coach Stage
one_liner: One Radix Themes design system with a dark live-call stage, a faceted persona library, an AI persona wizard and an evidence-first debrief.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed Radix Themes as the single design system: one Theme (teal accent, slate gray, medium radius) with Radix primitives for focus, keyboard and ARIA, so custom work stays accessible and low-debt. Changed three things. Radix Themes has no coaching HUD, score ring or persona dossier, so those are built on Radix primitives as one documented pattern set. The live call uses a dark stage surface, because a default light Radix shell reads as a template. Tailwind is removed after migration. Mobbin matches were mixed; the useful ones were SchoolAI, Klaviyo, Delphi, Tana and Descript. Self-scores: A 7.5, B 7.5, C 7, D 5.4, E 5.2; business F1 SaaS 4, F2 selling to entities 6, F3 not worth building 3.

ui_stack.name: Radix Themes 3 (@radix-ui/themes)
ui_stack.role: Design system: Theme tokens (accent, gray, radius, appearance), Card, Button, Badge, Callout, Tabs, SegmentedControl, Dialog, Slider, Progress, Table, DataList, Avatar.
ui_stack.why: Accessible by default and needs little custom CSS, so design debt stays low.

ui_stack.name: Radix Primitives (radix-ui: Accordion, Toast, Popover, Form)
ui_stack.role: Behaviour layer under the coach rail, whisper toasts, debrief accordion and wizard forms.
ui_stack.why: Focus management and ARIA for the custom live HUD, where Radix Themes has no component.

ui_stack.name: Recharts
ui_stack.role: The only chart library: score trends, donut, sparklines and the weekly heatmap.
ui_stack.why: Single chart dependency; colors come from Radix tokens so light and dark match.

ui_stack.name: Motion (motion/react)
ui_stack.role: Whisper entrance, rubric bar fill and score ring draw.
ui_stack.why: Declarative, with a built-in reduced-motion path.

ui_stack.name: cmdk
ui_stack.role: Command palette (⌘K) over personas, scenarios and past calls.
ui_stack.why: Keyboard-first navigation without a custom search widget.

ui_stack.name: lucide-react, zod, Radix Form
ui_stack.role: Icons; zod validates persona JSON in CI and the wizard forms at runtime.
ui_stack.why: Keeps existing icons and zod; one validation schema for files and forms.

palette.use: Primary buttons, active tabs, the Start button on pre-call.
Accent text on light surfaces, with AA contrast on slate 1.
Light app background for Library, Debrief, Progress and Team.
Body and headings on light surfaces.
Live call and landing hero surface with a faint teal tint; panels on it are #161B1F.

design_language.typography: Sora 600 for display headings (keeps the current brand), Inter 400/500 for UI and transcript (15/24 on stage, 16/24 on light), Geist Mono for timers, scores and rubric weights with tabular numerals. Radix Themes size scale 1-9, headings at -0.02em tracking, loaded with next/font.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radix radius medium (6px controls), 12px cards, 20px for the live dock. Hairline borders from slate 6 replace soft shadows on light. On stage, panels are solid layers with 1px white-8% borders. Each screen has one elevated element: the dock or the active coach card.
design_language.motion: Whisper cues rise 8px and fade in over 180ms, one at a time, auto-dismissing after 8s unless hovered. Rubric bars fill with a spring. The voice ring is a 30fps canvas driven by audio level, not a looping decoration. prefers-reduced-motion turns all movement into opacity changes.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.5px stroke, 16px in controls and 20px in cards. Persona avatars are monograms on a hue from the Radix accent scale, chosen by name hash. No emoji in product UI.
design_language.theme_modes: Light by default for Library, Debrief, Progress and Team. Dark stage for the live call and landing hero, using Theme appearance='dark' with the stage token. The shell follows prefers-color-scheme (appearance='inherit'), with a manual toggle in the avatar menu.

navigation_and_ia: Top bar: Practice, Library, Progress, Team (role-gated), a primary 'New persona' button and a ⌘K trigger. Routes: / (landing), /library (facet rail and grid), /library/new (wizard), /practice/[id] (pre-call), /call/[id] (live), /debrief/[id], /progress, /team. Mobile uses a bottom tab bar (Practice, Library, Progress, More). Sign-in, MFA and access code move under one avatar menu. Demo mode shows a small 'Demo' badge in the header instead of a full-width banner.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Coach loop: after each rep turn, a small OpenAI model reads the last few turns against the scenario's talk track and rubric and emits at most one whisper, which must cite the exact transcript line it reacted to. Target latency is under 2s; past 3s the rail shows 'Coach is thinking' and the call never blocks. Coach level (Off, Light, Full) sets whisper frequency and whether objection alerts show. Talk-track steps auto-check. Rubric criteria move from tentative (one weak span) to confirmed (two spans or one strong span), so the live score never overstates. The persona is not told about the coach, and grading stays a separate pass. Self-score D: 5.4. The design exceeds baseline only once the coach loop ships; today the app has none.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library ships as versioned JSON files in the repo, one per persona (role, industry, difficulty, objection tags, talk track, rubric weights, voice id, provenance), validated by zod in CI. Seed target: about 120 personas across the 14 sales jobs in the brief, human-reviewed before merge. Facets: sales job, industry, difficulty, objection type, channel (voice or text). Wizard: Source (job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or pasted call), then Extract (streaming field cards with evidence and confidence), then Shape (editable persona, rubric weights summing to 100), then Dry run (90-second text call), then Publish locally or open a prefilled PR. Low-confidence fields get a Callout. Self-score E: 5.2. The design meets baseline, but the realised score stays below 5 until the seed library ships (three built-ins today).
signature_moments: Cited whispers: every coach cue quotes the transcript line it reacted to, so the rep can check the coach.
Rubric fill: criteria bars fill as evidence lands, tentative first and confirmed later.
Model receipt: each debrief states which OpenAI model graded it, with latency and cost.
Edit on GitHub: every persona dossier opens a prefilled PR draft.
Dossier cards: persona cards styled like a briefing file, with difficulty shown as signal bars.
openai_fund_angle: 1) The OpenAI Realtime API becomes a first-class voice provider beside ElevenLabs; the pre-call panel offers it as a named option with the model visible. 2) Every model call is labelled in the UI (grader, coach, persona wizard), and a Settings > Models page shows per-call cost. 3) A Grader Lab page compares rubric agreement across models and invites contributors to submit eval cases. 4) A contribution path: good-first-issue labels on library personas, an AGENTS.md so Codex CLI contributors get repo rules, and a persona PR template validated by CI. 5) Credit the stack honestly: 'Built with OpenAI models' in the footer, and 'Reviewed with Codex' only once Codex PR review is actually running on this repo.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (about a week): add @radix-ui/themes, wrap the app in one Theme (accent teal, gray slate, radius medium), turn off Tailwind preflight, and map the five legacy classes to Radix components. Phase 2: rebuild Pre-call, Debrief and Dashboard. Phase 3: live cockpit and coach loop, with the mobile sheet. Phase 4: persona JSON library, zod validation in CI, and the wizard. Phase 5: Progress, Team and the dark stage theme. Remove Tailwind last, once no class references remain.

risks: Tailwind 3 and Radix Themes CSS can clash on preflight and tokens during migration; keep both until the last phase and diff screenshots per screen.
Default-Radix look: mitigate with the stage surface, the voice ring and the teal accent. Without a distinctive live cockpit, reviewers may still read it as a template.
Coach latency and cost: per-turn classification with an OpenAI model adds spend and lag. Cap whispers per minute and use the smallest model that passes eval.
Persona quality: about 120 seeded personas need human review. Generated personas can carry stereotypes, so mark provenance and review sensitive industries such as insurance and collections.
Live HUD accessibility: whispers need throttled aria-live announcements and a keyboard path to dismiss; reduced motion must disable the voice ring.
Business: the market is crowded (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Outdoo, Mindtickle, Yoodli). The open-source core earns value through hosted team features and call-center licensing, not seats alone.
